document.title: Certificate of Entitlement (CE) - UNJSPF webpage (incl. 2026 CE exercise FAQ)

chunks.heading: What is the Certificate of Entitlement (CE) exercise?
chunks.text: Each year the Fund conducts an exercise to verify the continuing eligibility of retirees and beneficiaries to the benefits they are receiving. As part of this exercise, each person in receipt of a benefit from the Fund must annually submit a Certificate of Entitlement (CE) to the Fund, provided their benefit was implemented before 29 June of that given year.

chunks.heading: How to submit the CE: Digital CE App option
chunks.text: Since 2021, retirees and beneficiaries can complete the CE exercise using the Digital CE App instead of submitting a paper CE. To submit a Digital CE, download the app, complete the enrolment process, and issue a Digital CE for current and future years using the app with biometric data collection. If you complete the CE through the Digital CE App, no paper form is needed. If the Digital CE isn't issued by June, the Fund will mail a paper CE and make it available in MSS (if not paid on the two-track); you then have two options — submit the paper CE (by mail or electronically via MSS) or submit your Digital CE — by December 31.

chunks.heading: How to submit the CE: paper-based option
chunks.text: There are two ways to get a paper-based CE: (1) the Fund mails paper CEs around June each year; (2) retirees and beneficiaries not on the two-track can also download their CE in MSS under the DOCUMENTS tab. The CE must be dated, signed, and returned with the original signature/thumbprint to the Fund by 31 December to avoid benefit suspension. Submission options: (a) Electronic submission via MSS — scan and upload the signed/dated form in PDF or JPEG using the 'Document Upload' feature; available even for those paid on the Two-Track. (b) Mailing the original CE form to the addresses on the Contact Us page. (c) Dropping it off in person at drop-boxes available at the Fund's New York and Geneva offices.

chunks.heading: 2026 CE exercise: who receives the form and when
chunks.text: The 2026 Certificates of Entitlement (CE) were sent to retirees and beneficiaries whose benefits started before 29 June 2026 and who hadn't completed their digital CE through the DCE App by that date. A second CE will be sent in October to those who haven't submitted their paper CE or completed their DCE through the app by then.

chunks.heading: 2026 CE exercise: required action and deadline
chunks.text: Beneficiaries and retirees with benefits implemented before 29 June 2026 must complete the CE exercise either via the DCE App or by submitting a paper CE with their original signature by 31 December 2026 to avoid benefit suspension. If no paper CE or DCE is submitted by that date, benefit payments may be suspended; benefits are reinstated retroactively only upon receipt of the required documentation.

chunks.heading: 2026 CE exercise: who will NOT receive a CE form
chunks.text: Beneficiaries and retirees whose benefits were not implemented before 29 June 2026 will not receive a 2026 paper CE and don't need to take any action for this exercise, though they can issue a DCE if desired. Compliance will be required for the next CE exercise starting at the end of June 2027. Beneficiaries and retirees who complete their digital CE using the DCE App by 29 June 2026 will also not receive a paper CE, as they will have met the 2026 CE requirements.

chunks.heading: 2026 CE exercise: handling duplicate CEs
chunks.text: If you receive multiple paper CEs for the same year, only one original, dated, and signed CE needs to be returned to the Fund (by mail or electronically via MSS) by the deadline. As long as the signature is acceptable, benefits will continue without interruption. If you complete the CE using the Digital CE app, no paper CE form needs to be submitted.

chunks.heading: What to do if you did not receive a paper CE and cannot access it in MSS
chunks.text: Send a letter to the Fund including your full name, official address, Unique ID (UID) and/or retirement number(s), the date, and your signature, using the subject line 'Non-receipt of the [year] CE.' Once received, it is added to your file to notify the Fund and help prevent a potential suspension of your benefits; the letter must be sent by 31 December of that year. Alternatively, complete the CE exercise using the Digital CE app, in which case no letter is needed.

chunks.heading: Keeping your address updated in the Fund's records
chunks.text: A common reason for missing a CE is a failure to update the mailing address. If you change your address permanently, update it online in MSS under the ADDRESS tab (if not paid on the two-track and neither the old nor new address is a pouch address). If you can't update it in MSS, complete, sign, and date the PF23/M form (available in MSS under the FORMS tab and on the Fund's website), and submit it by mail or electronically in MSS. Alternatively, send a letter with your full name, UID and/or retirement number(s), new address, phone number(s) in international format, email (if available), date, and signature. Changes are only made upon receipt of the ORIGINAL PF23/M form or letter, or through MSS — not via email or fax. You can update your email in MSS under the 'Account' tab; phone and emergency contacts require submission of PF23/M or a letter.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: when is the CE normally sent?
chunks.text: The Fund usually mails paper CEs at the end of June (1st Mailing) and again at the end of October (2nd Mailing) if no CE has been submitted by early October. Retirees and beneficiaries who are NOT on the two-track can also view and print their CE form in Member Self Service (MSS) under the DOCUMENTS tab.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: how to check if the CE has been received
chunks.text: Paper CE: once signed and returned (whether the mailed one or the MSS CE), you can track its receipt online under the 'Proof Documents' tab in the MSS portal — wait 4-6 weeks before checking due to processing volume; check again in a couple of weeks if not listed. Only original barcoded CEs from official mailings or printed from MSS can be tracked, not copies. Digital CE: check the DCE app, which will show the DCE is valid until December 31 of that year; you can also check its issuance online under the 'Proof Documents' tab in MSS.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: fax/email submissions and old forms not accepted
chunks.text: UNJSPF must receive an original CE from the current year's exercise either by mail or electronically through MSS for a benefit to continue in payment. No facsimiles, e-mails, or old forms from a prior year will be accepted. Alternatively, the CE exercise can be completed via the Digital CE app.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: what happens if the CE is not returned
chunks.text: If the CE is not returned to UNJSPF by 31 December of that year, the benefit will be suspended until the CE is returned or the Fund is provided with acceptable proof that the person is still alive.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: what to do if away from your home address
chunks.text: If NOT paid under the two-track: complete the CE exercise using the DCE app, download the CE from MSS under the documents tab, or (if preferring paper) ensure mail is forwarded, or if the CE hasn't arrived by July/November, write to UNJSPF for a new CE to be mailed and return it by mail or via MSS document upload. If paid under the two-track: you must spend at least six months of every year in your declared country of residence to be paid under the two-track for that country, so wait until back home to issue the DCE or mail the paper CE; if the CE hasn't arrived by July/November, write to UNJSPF for a new CE to be mailed and return it by mail or via MSS document upload.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: does the signature or thumbprint need to be authenticated?
chunks.text: Signature authentication is NOT REQUIRED if the signature on the CE form matches the original signature the Fund has on file (typically from original Payment Instructions) or a more recently received, duly authenticated signature. Authentication IS REQUIRED if the signature on the CE form notably differs from the original and no duly authenticated signature matches the new one. As a general rule, signature authentication is REQUIRED for each CE form or document with a thumbprint.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: authenticating a changed signature
chunks.text: If the signature on the CE form differs notably from the original signature on file, the Fund will require the retiree or beneficiary to have their signature authenticated by an official from any UNJSPF member organization (e.g., a Human Resources Officer), a UNJSPF official, a government official, or a notary public. The person authenticating must provide their full name, title, date, stamp/seal, signature, and (if applicable) their license or index number in the designated area on the CE form. Future signatures must match the authenticated signature.

chunks.heading: General FAQ: using a thumbprint instead of a signature
chunks.text: Signature authentication is required for each paper CE form with a thumbprint. If a retiree or beneficiary cannot sign due to ill health, they can use their thumbprint in the designated box, which must be authenticated by their attending physician (full name, title, stamp/seal, and signature). The physician must also issue a medical certificate in English or French, on official letterhead, attesting to the health condition preventing signing, attached to the authenticated CE form when submitted. If the same physician authenticates the thumbprint in subsequent years, no new medical certificate is needed; if a different doctor authenticates a future form, a new medical statement is required. For serious long-term health issues, the Fund recommends starting the process to appoint a legal guardian.
